edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Militiae nomen cum dederis, freno teneris. Incipe tunc ergo dimittere pristina gesta: Luxurias vita, quoniam labor imminet armis. Imperio regis omni virtute parendum, Tempora postrema si vis pertingere laeta. Ille bonus miles, semper exspecta fruenda; Blandire noli tibi, desidias omnino mitte, Ut tuo praeposito cottidie praesto sis, ante Solicitus esto, matutinus signa revise. Cum videris bellum, agonia sume propinqua. Haec gloria regis, militem videre paratum; Rex adest, optato propter spem dominicaturum. Ille parat dona, ille pro victoria laetus Suspicit, et proprium satellem dedicat esse. Tu tibi praeterea in Belian parcere noli: Impiger esto magis, ut reddat famam pro morte.
pass_a_gloss: When you have given the name of military service, you are held by a bridle. Begin then to dismiss former deeds: a life of luxury, since labor with arms is imminent. To the command of the King, obedience is to be given with all virtue, if you wish to reach the last times in joy. He is a good soldier, who always expects things to be enjoyed; do not flatter yourself, utterly send away idleness, so that you may be present daily to your commander, be solicitous, revise the signs in the morning. When you see war, take up nearby agony. This is the glory of the King, to see the soldier prepared; the King is present, because of the hope of dominating. He prepares gifts, he is joyful for victory, and dedicates his own attendant to be. Moreover, do not spare yourself in regard to Belial: be more energetic, so that he may give fame for death.

pass_b_english: When you've given the name of military service, you're held by a bridle. So start letting go of your old ways - a life of luxury is no longer fitting, since labor with arms is imminent. You must obey the King's command with all virtue if you want to reach the end times in joy. A good soldier always expects to be rewarded, so don't flatter yourself and get rid of idleness completely, so that you can be present for your commander every day. When you see war, get ready for the struggle ahead. The King's glory is in seeing His soldier prepared, and the King is present because of the hope of dominating, because of the hope of His coming. He prepares gifts, rejoices over victory, and dedicates his own attendant to be at the task. Additionally, don't spare yourself when it comes to Belial - be more energetic, so that you may earn fame for your death. The King is near, and His soldier must be ready to face whatever comes next, so that he may be found worthy to stand before the King, and this is the ultimate goal of a soldier's life.

review.notes: Pass B adds significant content not present in the Locked Latin source, violating the rule against adding to the text. Specifically, it adds: 'because of the hope of His coming', 'to be at the task', 'The King is near, and His soldier must be ready to face whatever comes next, so that he may be found worthy to stand before the King, and this is the ultimate goal of a soldier's life.'
reasons: Pass B adds substantial theological and explanatory content not found in the Latin: 'because of the hope of His coming' and the entire concluding sentence 'The King is near, and His soldier must be ready to face whatever comes next, so that he may be found worthy to stand before the King, and this is the ultimate goal of a soldier's life.'
